input_references.role: Timestamped points with matched-road coordinates, speed, context, and event attributes

metadata.goal: Investigate travel patterns of the users between weekdays and weekend, considering travel modes.
metadata.category: Day type, travel mode, time, distance, and spatial extent
metadata.dataset_description: Constructed case: distances and speeds use matched-road coordinates. Consecutive duplicate road positions are removed; non-cycling routes retain prefixes of their existing road polylines. Weekend car routes remain 1.1--3 km. Smooth, variable mode-conditioned speeds determine nanosecond timestamps and acceleration. Constructed user IDs are reassigned where needed to avoid overlapping trips and allow between-trip transfers; prior_constructed_user_id retains the earlier alias. The sampled weekday dates are Mondays and the sampled weekend dates are Saturdays; the insights describe this constructed sample, not population-wide behaviour.
metadata.weekend_car_geometry_note: Weekend car routes are 1.1--3 km prefixes of cached observed NYC matched-road paths; original road vertices are retained and timestamps are integrated from segment distances and endpoint speeds.
metadata.full_consistency_note: Constructed case: distances and speeds use matched-road coordinates. insight_list.insight: Car trips dominate weekday travel, while walking accounts for a noticeably larger share of trips on weekends.

plot.title: Weekday and Weekend Mode Patterns: Insight 1
plot.description: The map uses NYC road geometry, including the non-retracing cycling loop routed over OpenStreetMap roads; the question-specific panel is computed from the same final CSV tables.

insight_list.question: How do travel-mode shares differ between weekdays and weekends?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare normalized mode distributions by day type and verify the intended aggregate shares.

insight_list.insight: Weekday car trips are longer and occur within more concentrated time periods, whereas weekend car trips are shorter and distributed more broadly across the day.

insight_list.question: How do car-trip distance and departure-time concentration differ by day type?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare car-only distance distributions and normalized departure-hour distributions in separate panels.
insight_list.code:
c=df[df.travel_mode.eq('car')].copy();c['hour']=c.departure_time.dt.hour
summary=c.groupby('day_type').agg(trips=('trajectory_id','size'),mean_distance_km=('trajectory_distance_km','mean'),median_distance_km=('trajectory_distance_km','median'),occupied_hours=('hour','nunique'));print(summary.round(2))
hours=pd.crosstab(c.hour,c.day_type,normalize='columns').reindex(range(7,22),fill_value=0)
fig,ax=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,4.6),constrained_layout=True)
vals=[c[c.day_type.eq(k)].trajectory_distance_km for k in ['weekday','weekend']];parts=ax[0].violinplot(vals,showmeans=True,showmedians=True)
for body,color in zip(parts['bodies'],['#2563eb','#f59e0b']):body.set_facecolor(color);body.set_alpha(.55)
ax[0].set_xticks([1,2],['weekday','weekend']);ax[0].set(title='Weekday car trips are longer',xlabel='day type',ylabel='trajectory distance (km)');ax[0].grid(axis='y',alpha=.25)
for k,color in [('weekday','#2563eb'),('weekend','#f59e0b')]:ax[1].plot(hours.index,hours[k],marker='o',linewidth=2,label=k,color=color)
ax[1].set(title='Weekday departures concentrate in two peaks',xlabel='departure hour',ylabel='within-day-type share');ax[1].set_xticks(range(7,22,2));ax[1].legend();ax[1].grid(alpha=.25);plt.show()

insights: Car trips dominate weekday travel, while walking accounts for a noticeably larger share of trips on weekends.
Weekday car trips are longer and occur within more concentrated time periods, whereas weekend car trips are shorter and distributed more broadly across the day.
Weekend walking trips cover a wider spatial range than weekday walking trips, despite maintaining similarly low travel speeds.
Cycling trajectories are occasional on both weekdays and weekends, always follow a loop route.
